query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing Cr content in a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating promotes the in-situ formation of a continuous, adherent Cr₂O₃ tribo-oxide layer during high-temperature sliding, which acts as a protective barrier that lowers overall wear rate and suppresses subsurface plastic deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Fe20Ni20Cr20Co20Cu20 HEA coating (5 µm thick) on a conventional steel substrate
generation.intervention: Adjust composition to Fe18Ni18Cr30Co17Cu17 (Cr increased to 30 at%, Cu reduced to 17 at%)
generation.conditions: Dry sliding, 10 N normal load, 0.01 m/s sliding speed, 600 °C in air (pO₂≈0.21 atm)
generation.structural_mediator: Thickness and continuity of the Cr₂O₃ tribo-oxide scale formed on the contact surface
generation.mechanism: A thicker, coherent Cr₂O₃ layer reduces adhesive junction growth and plastic flow at asperities, leading to lowered material removal and smaller subsurface deformation zones
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the equiatomic baseline, the Cr-enriched coating will exhibit a decreased wear rate and reduced subsurface plastic deformation under the same sliding conditions
generation.baseline: Equiatomic Fe20Ni20Cr20Co20Cu20 coating under identical sliding test
generation.boundary: Predictions valid in the high-temperature sliding regime of 500–700 °C in air; may not hold in inert or humid environments
generation.uncertainty: Moderate – depends on scale adherence and possible competing oxide phases

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of coated steel discs (equiatomic and Cr-enriched). Perform reciprocating sliding in air at 600 °C, 10 N, 0.01 m/s for a fixed sliding distance. Characterize wear by mass loss and cross-sectional SEM/EDS to measure oxide scale thickness and subsurface deformation layer thickness.
measurements: Subsurface plastic deformation zone thickness (µm) by metallographic cross-section
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if the Cr-enriched coating does not show both (a) ≥20% reduction in wear rate and (b) a thicker (>20%) Cr₂O₃ scale relative to baseline, or if wear reduction occurs without a corresponding increase in oxide scale thickness.
